text:
june: Hey - CI deploys to staging started failing ~30m ago. All jobs that call the deploy service are getting 403/insufficient_scope. Nothing in the app code changed.
alex: saw that too on my pipeline. Fails during the `deploy` step. Short log attached from a failing run.
june: paste of failing curl from the runner:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/deploy \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ya29.XXXXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"env":"staging","version":"sha-abc123"}'
```
response:
```json
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "message": "token missing required scope: deploy.write"
}
```

samir: interesting — this is the service-account token used by the CI bot, right? `service-account:ci-deployer-bot`?
june: yes. That bot's keys are managed via the infra rotation service. The deploy permission hasn't changed in our rollout rules AFAIK.
jen: I just checked the repo's terraform IAM binding for `ci-deployer-bot` — it had role `roles/ci.deployer` which maps to `deploy.write`. No recent terraform changes in the last week.

alex: ops-bot can you check rotation logs for that SA? @ops-bot
ops-bot: Rotation job summary:
- 2026-03-01 02:00 UTC: key created (k-01)
- 2026-03-08 02:00 UTC: key rotated (k-02)
- 2026-03-15 01:20 UTC: policy tightened (minimum scopes enforcement enabled)
- 2026-03-15 02:05 UTC: rotated key (k-03) -> active

samir: ahhh. "minimum scopes enforcement enabled" — that policy strips scopes not explicitly allowed by an allowlist at rotation time. Looks like the rotation job issued a token with only a subset of scopes.
june: can someone confirm what scopes k-03 actually got?

jen: pulled the rotation audit entry: scopes on k-03 = ["ci.read","artifact.read","deploy.read"] (no `deploy.write`). That explains the 403.
alex: why would it drop deploy.write? terraform binding shows role present. Could be a bug in the rotation allowlist service (it reads per-project allowlist, then intersects with requested scopes). If the CI pipeline requests a broad token, rotation may enforce the smaller set.

samir: for immediate mitigation we have two options: (1) temporarily issue an emergency key k-04 with full deploy.write scope (manual create) and update pipeline secret, or (2) modify the pipeline to use the older key if still present (k-02) — but k-02 was revoked by rotation. Manual key is faster.
june: we need the minimal blast radius. If we create k-04, rotate/schedule deletion after next safe window. Also add an allowlist entry for `ci-deployer-bot`.
jen: I'm creating a manual key now with deploy.write and pushing to the protected secrets location. Will tag it `temp/ci-deploy-k04`.

alex: quick repro for the team to validate once k-04 is up:
```
# from a build runner
export REDWOOD_TOKEN=REDACTED_K04
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/deploy -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" -d '{"env":"staging","version":"sha-abc123"}' | jq .
```

ops-bot: manual key k-04 created by jen at 1768005340 and stored in secrets path `secret/ci/ci-deployer-bot/k04-temp`. KeyID=k-04. Audit: created by jen.
june: patching the pipeline to use temp key now.

(10m pass)

alex: confirmed — pipelines using temp key succeed and staging deploys are green. Logs show 200 OK and deploy tasks proceeding.
samir: follow-up items:
- (P1) Fix rotation allowlist so it keeps `deploy.write` for `ci-deployer-bot` where terraform binds the role. Potential race: allowlist data is stale in rotation service cache.
- (P2) Add an integration test to rotation job to assert required roles/scopes for each known CI SA before revoking an old key.
- (P3) Short-term: extend monitoring/alerting on 403/insufficient_scope spikes for deploy endpoints and auto-create a slack incident if >5 failing pipelines in 10m.
- (P4) Evaluate moving CI runners to OIDC ephemeral tokens (recommended) to avoid long-lived key rotation pain — blocked by some self-hosted runner limitations.

jen: I've scheduled a follow-up meeting with infra and security to scope P1/P2. Setting tentative for 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC. Inviting samir, ops, june, alex, infra-secs.

june: for the support ticket we'll tell the customer: cause = service account key rotation enforcement dropped `deploy.write` scope due to a tightened allowlist. Mitigation applied = temporary key and pipeline updated; permanent fix planned.

alex: note for runbook: when rotation policy changes, rotation service must consult terraform/iam state or a source-of-truth mapping for SA->required-scopes. Current fail-case was stale allowlist cache.

samir: I'll open an infra bug and reference this thread and attach the rotation audit entries. bug: INFRA-4312. Assigning to infra-jen.
jen: assigning. INFRA-4312 created with summary "rotation allowlist dropped deploy.write for ci-deployer-bot -> CI deploy failures". links: <https://infra-tracker/redwood/INFRA-4312>

june: closing loop on the incident: staging deploys back to normal with k-04. Permanent remediation tracked in INFRA-4312. We'll rotate k-04 out after fix and ensure rotation produces a key with deploy.write. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident closed at 1768005620. Audit: temporary key used for 42 minutes.

alex: thanks everyone. quick retrospective: we should treat deploy scopes as high-sensitivity — put an allowlist mapping in SCM so rotation can't accidentally drop them. :+1:

jen: added follow-up checklist to INFRA-4312 including test vectors and a pre-rotation validation step.

june: ok I'm marking this thread resolved. If anyone sees further deploy 403s ping here.
